默认控图.text: - Round 5: I like the plan but you don't need the extra cheese of starting your ult from behind the pillar. You can ult safely from site and it will achieve the same results, without the downside of being alone on an island once it's done. How I see it: On defense, I dislike using my ultimate right off the gate with no info, because it's incredibly valuable and I'll be really disappointed if I don't see any enemies. I can't even count on having gained any significant map control because at the end it sends me all the way back to where I started. If I'm ulting, it's because I know a fight is coming, therefore I don't need to factor in the "max distance I can cover on foot while ulted" since I'm going to take a duel immediately at the first corner. Anyway, you're a little careless (and lucky that Jett misses her Op shot) on your way back to safety, but I like your off-angle hold afterwards. Later in the round when you realize they're coming B main, you should absolutely not be looking for a pick without your ultimate. I would have ulted from B-link straight away (which you did eventually, just make sure you don't feed your opponents a free chance of killing you before that). Good round overall.

Basically, it's just a skill you have to practice and develop while playing, but make sure you focus on trying to develop the skill and not just play without thinking. Maybe you already understand the concept, but the thing that defines whether you're "in danger" or not is map control and team vision. This means you need to be watching the minimap to see your teammates positions, see what vision they have,  and deduce from that all of the places that the enemy could be. Just for example, on ascent defense if you have a teammate watching mid from market, you don't have to worry about someone walking out from link up to cat, but if that teammate isnt playing far up enough to see high mid, you need to be understanding that an enemy could potentially walk from high mid up to short without being seen. And, for example, if you were in short holding cat in that situation, you need to have your crosshair positioned for a peek from the enemy 100% of time (until you reposition or need to turn attention to a main or something). To work on it in actual matches, focus on watching the minimap at all times that you know you are safe. i.e. the first 10 seconds or so of the round (as long as you arent peeking out lol) And then in addition, if you are holding an angle and want to check minimap, just pull away to the side of the angle for a bit, check the map, then move back to hold position. Hi. Your problem is that you play reactively instead of proactively. Your team is uncoordinated and you either win the round by killing 3 or watch your whole team die because you all went in without a plan. Your aim is good and your gunfight intuition is solid but you fail to put yourself in good positions and are forced to try and deal with whatever randomly happens in the round. Here's what to do instead: On attack, you need to be calling plays for your team. They can be simple (e.g. what you did on round 6 was good), but you almost never do this. 1. **You are playing way too aggressive as an initiator.** Honestly, the way you are aggressively taking space and pushing out it looks like you really should be playing a duelist. However, if you really want to stick with initiator, you need to stop pushing out so fast like this. Play behind your duelist, don't go into site first, and don't aggressively peek angles e.g. mid. You have no utility to escape like Jett or Reyna so you will be punished if you miss your shots.
  2. **Don't rush your utility.** Tejo's utility is very powerful, but you need to stop using it all in the span of 5 seconds. Take your time with the utility, place your missiles effectively, use your stun effectively etc. Our utility doesn't reset at the end of the round, so there is no need to use ultimate in a 4v2, or have your stun out in a 1v1 duel. Your aim is good, so use that to your advantage, don't rely too much on winning your fights through utility.
  3. **Stop lurking.** The whole point of playing initiator is to support your team, mainly your duelists, with utility to get onto site or to control site. If you lurk, all that utility is practically wasted as you can't support your team well. Tejo is an exception, as his utility is usable from afar, but you need to stop lurking and play with your team more as you are losing rounds where you could've traded out your teammates.
  4. **No crouch spray.** I don't want to see any crouch spraying from 50 metres away. This needs to be drilled into your he

Defense. Your job is to play off setup. If, however, you cannot, like the enemy is on the other site, you consider two things. 
  Is your team currently holding them off, or are they currently being held off? 
  How many enemies are spotted? If your team is **not** holding them off, then you rotate fast. Of course, you need to know how many there are, but typically, if your team is NOT holding them off, you know where about 4 enemies are, and 1 is unknown. Where you go is typically harder to answer, but a strong word of advice is that you, as the sentinel with no utility, will pick one side with more people. Your job is now just to either trade or be a living meat shield, do NOT go with the weak side unless you really feel like it. If your team **is** holding them off, then you have to consider #2. How many enemies are spotted? This is incredibly important. You're not just a sentinel to afk on site. You're there to take space and get kills. If you've spotted 4 enemies on B, while you're in A. That's a 1v1 at best. You take that to walk up and look for a fight. If, by god's grace, let's say you know where all FIVE enemies are, that's your holy grail. You can run and take as much space as you want. I like to run up to mid and take out one player before running away. You've basically won the round at this point AND gotten yourself a free kill.

If you want to get better at aiming you should aimtrain. I know its kind of a touchy subject on this discord but since you asked my personal opinion I think aimtraining consistently is very helpful and will noticeably improve your aim. Most of aim is unconscious. When you go into a deathmatch with the goal to "aim in X way during this deathmatch" it's really hard because you can't try to properly apply and adjust a skill you haven't practiced a lot in real time. Find a playlist or routine or a few scenarios you like and play them every day for 20-30 mins. Try to pay attention to weaknesses (tracking, flicking, smoothness, etc.) and push your high scores. You will notice yourself becoming more confident with your reactions and hitting easy- to medium- difficulty shots much more effortlessly in deathmatch and in game, which will let you actually focus on other aspects like being "patient/calm" while aiming. My caveat is this: 50/50s are always going to be 50/50s. Gunfights will get easier as your aim becomes better and they will get hard again when you rank up and face more formidable players. At the end of the day, unless your aim is ESPECIALLY good or bad, when you swing a dry 1v1, you WILL lose about half of the time. It's not because you panic sprayed or didn't have fast enough reaction time or didn't have "patient/calm" aim, it's because you TOOK a 50/50 and the coin landed face down. If you want to get better at aiming, practice your aiming. If you want to get better at g

1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.

On defense, you need to fight for space more proactively. Sitting backsite and waiting to see where the enemies push is almost always a bad idea unless you're playing cypher or killjoy. For smokes specifically (except viper), you almost always want to smoke somewhere at the start of the round and fight for it with 1-2 other teammates. On bind, smoke B long deep every round and fight it with one of your B players. If nobody is there, take the TP and crunch showers with one of your A players. If they come B, shoot them as they run through your smoke. For other maps, you can 1-way main or smoke mid (smoke tiles on ascent and double peek mid, smoke B main on sunset and fight it with a teammate, 1-way C on Lotus and have your jett or chamber go wide on mound, etc.). The key to this is that it gives you space and info, beyond just kill opportunities. If the enemies run through your smoke, you can kill them. If they don't, you have main smoked off so 1 person can hold it and you can play 3 people stacked on the other site. Primary takeaway: **You always want to have a PLAN for the round and ASK at least 1 teammate to DO something WITH you.** Hope this helps!

Defense. Your job is to play off setup. If, however, you cannot, like the enemy is on the other site, you consider two things. 
  Is your team currently holding them off, or are they currently being held off? 
  How many enemies are spotted? If your team is **not** holding them off, then you rotate fast. Where you go is typically harder to answer, but a strong word of advice is that you, as the sentinel with no utility, will pick one side with more people. ----------------- And specifically on jett, entry isn't quite as hard as you might think. I'm not super advanced into it but the general strategy is throw a cloudburst into the middle of the site (but close enough that you can dash to it) and dash into it right after it forms. From there you want to figure out if you saw anyone when you went in, then check your minimap briefly to see if your team is walking in or if they see someone. If you want to get better at aiming you should aimtrain. I know its kind of a touchy subject on this discord but since you asked my personal opinion I think aimtraining consistently is very helpful and will noticeably improve your aim. Most of aim is unconscious. When you go into a deathmatch with the goal to "aim in X way during this deathmatch" it's really hard because you can't try to properly apply and adjust a skill you haven't practiced a lot in real time. Find a playlist or routine or a few scenarios you like and play them every day for 20-30 mins. Try to pay attention to weaknesses (tracking, flicking, smoothness, etc.) and push your high scores. You will notice yourself becoming more confident with your reactions and hitting easy- to medium- difficulty shots much more effortlessly in deathmatch and in game, which will let you actually focus on other aspects like being "patient/calm" while aiming. My caveat is this: 50/50s are always going to be 50/50s. Gunfights will get easier as your aim becomes better and they will get hard again when you rank up and face more formidable players. At the end of the day, unless your aim is ESPECIALLY good or bad, when you swing a dry 1v1, you WILL lose about half of the time. It's not because you panic sprayed or didn't have fast enough reaction time or didn't have "patient/calm" aim, it's because you TOOK a 50/50 and the coin landed face down. If you want to get better at aiming, practice your aiming. If you want to get better at g

  2. Building on point 1, beware where your enemies can be: Look at the entry on round 11. Offense. Your job is to keep your utility up (most likely your flank utility) and hold space across a wide part of the map. My favorite word of advice as a lurker is that you can play *passive* lurk. Passive lurk effectively means just holding an angle and waiting. In ranked, people get jittery, people look for space. Remember how I said that you on defense need to look for space? Guess what, other sentinels or lurkers will do what you do and look for the 1v1. You're going to be taking it. I'll add an example real quickly. Aside from passive lurking, it's a gamble. Lurking is all about intuition and how confident you are in your aim. If you're not feeling your aim, you really shouldn't do much active lurking, and stick to passive. Let's say you passive lurk and don't find anything, then you consider two options. A. Does my team have any space and are they going to entry? **If yes.** Then your job now is to go back and help them OR consider a lurk through mid. **If no.** Your job now is either to go back and help them to FORCE a site, or to become an **active lurker.**

Defense. Your job is to play off setup. If, however, you cannot, like the enemy is on the other site, you consider two things. 
  Is your team currently holding them off, or are they currently being held off? 
  How many enemies are spotted? If your team is **not** holding them off, then you rotate fast. Of course, you need to know how many there are, but typically, if your team is NOT holding them off, you know where about 4 enemies are, and 1 is unknown. Where you go is typically harder to answer, but a strong word of advice is that you, as the sentinel with no utility, will pick one side with more people. Your job is now just to either trade or be a living meat shield, do NOT go with the weak side unless you really feel like it. If your team **is** holding them off, then you have to consider #2. How many enemies are spotted? This is incredibly important. You're not just a sentinel to afk on site. You're there to take space and get kills. If you've spotted 4 enemies on B, while you're in A. That's a 1v1 at best. You take that to walk up and look for a fight. If, by god's grace, let's say you know where all FIVE enemies are, that's your holy grail. You can run and take as much space as you want. I like to run up to mid and take out one player before running away. You've basically won the round at this point AND gotten yourself a free kill.
